Question: Let \(f(x)=10^{10x},\) \(g(x)=\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{10}\right),\) \(h_1(x)=g(f(x)),\) and \(h_n(x)=h_1(h_{n-1}(x))\) for integers \(n\ge2.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(h_{2011}(1)?\)
Solution:
First simplify the composition so that we can see what each iteration does. Since \(10^{10x}>0\) for every real \(x\), the logarithm is always defined, and
\[
h_1(x)=\log_{10}\left(\frac{10^{10x}}{10}\right)
=\log_{10}(10^{10x-1})=10x-1.
\]
Thus all the iterates are defined.

Let \(a_n=h_n(1)\). Then \(a_1=9\), and each subsequent term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 10 and subtracting 1. The first few terms are
\[
9,\quad89,\quad889,\quad8889.
\]
To justify this pattern, multiplying a number ending in 9 by 10 makes its ending 90. Subtracting 1 changes that ending to 89, leaving every earlier digit unchanged. Each step therefore adds one more 8 before the final 9.

Consequently, \(a_n\) consists of \(n-1\) copies of 8 followed by 9. The requested digit sum is
\[
2010\cdot8+9=\boxed{16{,}089},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
